A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same uncertainty-propagation and exploration framework, despite renaming OP2E to E-MCTS and substantially revising the experiments. All 17 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–C, support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original multi-seed experiments on Slide and Mountain Car, including training-component ablations in Figures 1–2.

after.justification: V2 reports original Deep Sea experiments using three transition-model configurations, with learning curves, exploration coverage and goal-discovery results in Figure 1 and Table 1.

M1.justification: The propagation framework remains, but v2 replaces ensemble-based or count-and-rollout uncertainty estimation with RND or counts locally and a learned UBE head at leaves. It adds UBE training targets and reconstruction-trained model variants. V1's explicit double-planning and max-target construction is no longer presented, while separate exploration/exploitation episodes remain.

E1.justification: Slide and Mountain Car, including the modified Mountain Car reward setting used for ablations, are removed. V2 evaluates only the 40-by-40 Deep Sea environment, with randomized action mappings and penalties for movement toward the goal. This replaces the task coverage and removes continuous-state evaluation.

E2.justification: V1's main comparison uses vanilla MuZero against OP2E variants. V2 adds an evaluated only-UBE deep-exploration baseline alongside uninformed Alpha/MuZero exploration for each model configuration. Only-UBE still uses MCTS for value estimation but propagates exploration uncertainty through learning, providing a substantially different comparator.

E3.justification: The replacement experiments introduce true, abstracted and anchored model configurations and goal-discovery and exploration-coverage metrics. Reported settings also change substantially: MCTS simulations become 50 rather than 30/200, batch size becomes 256 rather than 128, and value-target TD length becomes 5 rather than 50. These are different experimental protocols, not matched reruns.

E4.justification: V1 Section 4.1 and Figure 2 separately test value targets, policy targets, alternating episodes and double planning. These controlled ablations are removed, including the test of exploration/exploitation episode separation retained in v2. Neither v2's main text nor its appendices supplies corresponding training-component ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions show means with standard-error bands. V1 uses 10 seeds for main results and 5 for ablations; v2 reports 5 for most settings and 10 for anchored-model E-MCTS and only-UBE. V2 additionally reports standard deviations for goal-discovery times in Table 1. These counts concern replacement experiments, not increased replication of retained results.

E6.justification: V1's Slide/Mountain Car performance and ablation findings are replaced by Deep Sea results. V2 Table 1 reports E-MCTS/only-UBE mean steps to goal of 7,279/19,167 with the true model, 17,871/33,539 with the abstracted model, and 14,119/24,101 with the anchored model. These are newly reported outcomes, not performance gains under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: The Taylor-based propagation derivation, independence assumption and Appendix A proof are retained. V2 corrects the terminal-value discount from gamma^T in v1 Eq. 3 to gamma^(T-k) in Eq. 4 and revises the action-value variance expression to explicitly include local reward variance in Eqs. 11–12. The underlying theoretical framework remains substantially intact.

C1.justification: V1 presents uncertainty propagation, exploratory planning and stabilizing exploratory training as three contributions. V2 centers two contributions: E-MCTS uncertainty estimation and planning-based exploration, now claiming an advantage over UBE-only exploration with provided and learned models. Claims about improved training stability and final policies from max-target modifications disappear.

C2.justification: V2 Section 3.3 adds a substantive explanation of latent-state collapse and why novelty in abstract representations may fail to reflect environmental novelty. It conditions applicability on reliable uncertainty access and explains anchoring and UBE training as responses. This replaces much of v1's interpretation of target-generation stability and categorical-ensemble uncertainty problems.

D1.justification: The implementation basis changes from muzero-general to EfficientZero. V2 documents RND training, UBE targets and losses, Deep Sea encoding, and revised architectures and hyperparameters in Appendices B–C. It also specifies GPU models, 16 CPU cores, 100 GB RAM and 12–65 hours per seed, substantially extending v1's distributed-CPU hardware disclosure.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning against uncertainty-aware planning through Moerland et al., POMCP, POMCPOW, BOMCP and Stochastic MuZero. Its Plan2Explore discussion adds the role of latent disagreement and reconstruction in avoiding representation collapse. UBE moves from related discussion and a suggested combination to a central methodological and experimental reference.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and substantial portions of the background and discussion are rewritten. OP2E becomes E-MCTS, related work moves before experiments, and the former training-modification section is replaced by uncertainty-estimation challenges. Appendices B–C are extensively reorganized around the revised implementation.

P2.justification: V1's two-panel performance figure and four-panel ablation figure are replaced by a six-panel model-by-metric figure and a goal-discovery table. Appendix architectures and settings are reorganized into three tables, replacing the earlier parameter and temperature displays. The manuscript also changes its title, heading and running-header layout.

improvement.justification: V2 provides a more diagnostic test of the central planning claim by comparing against UBE-only exploration with corresponding model and uncertainty choices. Its explicit treatment of unreliable abstract-state uncertainty and fuller implementation disclosures also improve clarity and assessability. These gains are tempered by losing continuous-state evaluation and no longer ablating the retained exploration/exploitation split, making the net improvement limited.
